items.stem: What does it mean for an ecosystem to be stable?

options.text: It stays in balance even as its parts change

items.explanation: Stability is a dynamic balance. Populations rise and fall, but the whole system stays in balance over time.

items.stem: Which of these is a limiting factor for a population?
items.explanation: A limiting factor restricts how large a population can grow. Food, water, space, and predators are limiting factors.

items.stem: The largest population of a species that an ecosystem can support over time is its...
items.explanation: Carrying capacity is the largest population an ecosystem can support over time, set by its limiting factors.

items.stem: In a predator-prey cycle, what usually happens right after the prey population grows large?
items.explanation: When prey are plentiful, predators have more food, so the predator population grows in response.

items.stem: Which of the following is a natural disturbance?
items.explanation: A wildfire is a natural disturbance. Highways, pollution, and invasive species are human-caused disturbances.

items.stem: Why can an invasive species harm an ecosystem so easily?

options.text: It cannot reproduce in the new area
It often has no natural predators there

items.explanation: With no natural predators in its new home, an invasive species can spread quickly and crowd out native species.

options.text: The variety of different species in an ecosystem
The total number of rocks in an area
The amount of sunlight reaching the ground
The age of the oldest tree

items.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of different species living in an ecosystem.

items.stem: Why are ecosystems with high biodiversity usually more resilient?

options.text: They have fewer species to worry about
Other species can fill the role of a lost one
They do not depend on sunlight

items.explanation: With many species doing many jobs, the loss of one can often be covered by another, so the system recovers more easily.

items.stem: The wolves in Yellowstone are an example of a keystone species because...

options.text: They are the largest animals in the park
So many other species depend on their effects
They live only near the rivers
They eat plants instead of animals

items.explanation: A keystone species has effects so large that its loss or return reshapes the whole ecosystem, as the wolves did.

items.stem: When wolves returned to Yellowstone, the chain of change that spread through the food web is called a...
items.explanation: A trophic cascade is a chain reaction that spreads through a food web from the top down, as the wolves set off in Yellowstone.
